KO.why: The committee backs KO as the lead staples name: a fresh break to a new high on 1.61 times its average volume, the strongest of the beverage names.

ABBV.why: A leading drug maker that dipped back to its breakout, held it and closed near the top of the day on 1.56 times average volume.
ABBV.contested: The committee splits on whether one strong daily bar after a choppy run is enough; it clears if the next daily close is another strong, non-red bar before the hourly buy is taken.

CAH.why: The committee rates CAH the best base in the room: a breakout from a tight base to a new high, closing at the top of the day.
CAH.contested: The committee splits on a choppy daily trend with the pace of the advance slowing; it clears if a second strong, non-red daily bar prints before the hourly buy is taken.

GLBE.why: A fast-growing cross-border e-commerce name at a new high, closing at the very top of the day on 1.54 times average volume.
GLBE.contested: The committee splits on buying an extension 13.3% above the 20-day average rather than a test; it clears if price pulls back to the breakout area and prints a strong bar there first.

MFC.why: An insurer breaking to a new high on 1.63 times average volume, the day after it dipped under its rising trendline and closed back above it.
MFC.contested: The committee splits on a daily trend with only one strong bar after a run of middling ones; it clears if a second strong, non-red daily bar prints before the hourly buy is taken.

CCEP.why: The second beverage name beside KO: a new high on heavy buying, and it has beaten the market by more than KO over the last month.
CCEP.contested: The committee splits on the last hourly candle, which closed red in the middle of its range; it clears on an hourly bar that closes in the top third of its range on 1.2 times normal volume.

BBY.why: The strongest relative strength of the ten advances: a retailer at a new high, closing at the top of the day after a sharp one-day shakeout.
BBY.contested: The committee splits on breakout volume of 1.31 times average, under the 1.4 times bar; it clears if the session that triggers the hourly buy closes at or above that bar.

DG.why: A discount retailer that keeps gaining on down days and broke out on a wide bar at 1.68 times average volume, closing near the day's high.
DG.contested: The committee splits on long-term averages still crossed the wrong way and a buy line at the top of its channel; it clears if the 100-day average closes back above the 200-day and the entry sits near yesterday's close.

BALL.why: A packaging maker breaking out of a long sideways base about 1% under its high on 1.6 times average volume, closing at the top of the day.
BALL.contested: The committee splits on flat moving averages and relative strength just under the leadership floor; it clears if the 50-day average climbs back above the 100-day and relative strength reaches that floor.

USFD.why: USFD was considered as a leader near its high on 2.41 times average volume, then dropped because its trigger buys before the new high prints.
USFD.contested: The committee rejected a buy 1.58% under the recent high that chases a stock far above its value area; it changes if the trigger becomes an hourly close above the recent high on expanding volume.

KDP.why: A beverage leader just under its 52-week high on 1.75 times average volume, held because its deal status as the buyer of JDE Peet's is unclear.
KDP.contested: The committee splits on timing, between waiting for an hourly close above the last pivot high and buying over yesterday's high or on a test; it clears once the deal status is resolved and an hourly close above 37.32 prints.

WCN.why: A waste hauler at a new high on 2.11 times average volume and rising on every chart, after a dip under its rising trendline was bought back.
WCN.contested: The committee splits on a chase 16.6% above the 20-day average with no pullback to buy; it clears if price pulls back to the breakout area and turns up there on a strong bar.

ADP.why: A group leader in an established weekly uptrend with strong relative strength, sitting 1.9% under its recent high of 309.4.
ADP.contested: The committee splits on the entry, an hourly break of the high against a daily close through it or a pullback to the 20-day average; it clears on a daily close above the recent high.

PK.why: A leader coiled 1.05% under its pivot at 17.14, with the weekly chart above its last swing high and the averages lined up in order.
PK.contested: The committee splits on buying an hourly close at the top of the day's range against a daily close through 17.14 or a pullback to the 20-day average; it clears on a daily close above the pivot.

SONY.why: The top technology name in this round: a leader with its averages lined up in order and the weekly chart 2.7% above its last swing high.
SONY.contested: The committee splits on a broken short-term trend with only one strong bar and an hourly trigger instead of a daily break of 26.31; it clears on a second strong daily close and a daily close above that line.

V.why: V is held at a new high on 1.48 times average volume with strong relative strength, so the committee keeps it and adds nothing at this price.
V.contested: The committee splits on how to add, on a pullback to the 20-day average or a buy over each new prior-day high; it clears on a daily close above a new pivot from a fresh base, with the gain protected by a tight trail.

NCNO.why: NCNO was considered for its ordered averages and strong relative strength 0.26% under its 23.5 pivot, then dropped because an hourly trigger can count a poke that fails.
NCNO.contested: The committee rejected an hourly poke through the pivot while the weekly chart is still under its swing high; it changes on a daily close above 23.5 on at least 1.4 times average volume.

BMY.why: BMY was considered on a fresh daily break over its swing high at 63.59 in a leading sector, then dropped because the weekly chart is 6.48% under its own swing high.
BMY.contested: The committee rejected a buy over yesterday's high on light volume with relative strength under the leadership floor; it changes on a weekly close above 68.64 on at least 1.4 times average volume.

CRBG.why: CRBG was considered on a fresh new high 1.7% above its 35.64 pivot on both the weekly and daily charts, then dropped because the break came on light volume.
CRBG.contested: The committee rejected a trigger with no volume test after a break on 1.08 times average volume, with a pending merger unresolved; it changes on a follow-through new high on at least 1.4 times average volume.

TAK.why: TAK was considered as an established weekly uptrend in a leading sector, then dropped because the committee would not buy a dip to the 20-day average.
TAK.contested: The committee rejected buying the dip itself while the weekly chart sits 10.3% past its swing high on average volume; it changes on a daily close above the 21.22 pivot on expanding volume.
